key_insight: When chest radiographs and clinical photographs conflicted, frontier models often hallucinated photograph findings that supported the radiograph-based diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight a reliability concern for medical AI that combines imaging with clinical photographs: conflicting evidence may be forced into an unsupported unifying diagnosis.
method: Paired real chest radiographs with synthetic clinical photographs across multiple conditions.
Created matched and mismatched pairs using the same radiograph while varying photograph findings.
Evaluated three frontier models for clinically significant hallucinations.
evidence_signal: Models hallucinated clinically significant photograph findings in 45–57.5% of mismatched pairs, versus 25–37.5% when the same photographs were shown alone.
watch_item: This synthetic, adversarial benchmark exposes failure modes but does not establish their frequency in routine clinical practice.
paper_title: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Evaluation of Multimodal Medical Reasoning with Synthetic Images
